answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a stake-and-reputation bond: every identity locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove fraud, so creating fake agents costs real money. Like an island community, trust is earned slowly; a whisper of bad behavior travels fast through shared attestations, and a glacier of accumulated honest history cannot be faked overnight. The attacker must pay the bond for each fake identity and lose it on detection, making mass fakery unprofitable.
